claim: CPython 3.13 does not remove the GIL by default; free-threaded mode is experimental and requires a separate build/executable
sub_question: Is the Python GIL removed by default in CPython 3.13?
evidence: Official 3.13 what's-new states free-threaded mode is experimental and not enabled by default; default builds keep the GIL.
quote_or_anchor: CPython now has experimental support for running in a free-threaded mode, with the global interpreter lock (GIL) disabled. This is an experimental feature and therefore is not enabled by default.
notes: Contradiction class: popular summaries sometimes imply GIL is gone in 3.13; primary docs say opt-in experimental only.

claim: The canonical configure flag for free-threaded / no-GIL CPython is --disable-gil
sub_question: What is the canonical configuration flag?
evidence: Docs state free-threaded builds come from official freethreaded installers or building with --disable-gil.
quote_or_anchor: or CPython can be built from source with the --disable-gil option.

claim: PEP 703 governs optional GIL / free-threading and keeps GIL as the default for CPython builds and python.org downloads
sub_question: What PEP governs free-threading / optional GIL?
source_title: PEP 703 – Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython
evidence: PEP 703 abstract and build-configuration section define --disable-gil and state GIL remains default.
quote_or_anchor: The global interpreter lock will remain the default for CPython builds and python.org downloads. A new build configuration flag, --disable-gil will be added to the configure script that will build CPython with support for running without the global interpreter lock.
notes: Python-Version on PEP is 3.13; resolution dated 24-Oct-2023.
